pool.text: Saskatoon was founded as a Temperance colony by the Toronto-based Temperance Colonization Society.
Saskatoon incorporated as a city, absorbing the communities of Saskatoon, Riversdale, and Nutana.
The Capitol Theatre opened in Saskatoon featuring the first talking movie exhibition.
Marquis Downs at Prairieland Park began hosting live horse racing until its closure.
Innovation Place was founded as a science and technology park bringing together numerous industries.
Lions Skatepark was constructed and opened within the Riversdale area of the city.
The historic Roxy Theatre reopened following a period of sitting unused for over a decade.
The Capitol 4 movie theatre shut down permanently in the downtown core area.
The NASCAR Canadian Tire Series made its inaugural stop at the racing track.
The museum design won the prestigious Award of Excellence from Canadian Architect magazine.
Construction of the city ring road Circle Drive concluded with the South project.
The Rush lacrosse team relocated to Saskatoon from Edmonton and achieved immediate success.
The Remai Modern opened to the public and received major international travel recognition.
Jim Pattison Children's Hospital opened under the auspices of the Saskatoon Health Region.
River Landing Towers completed construction featuring residential and office spaces.
The Saskatoon Berries joined the Western Canadian Baseball League as an expansion team.
FlixBus started operating daily transportation rides connecting Saskatoon with other prairie hubs.
